targets.title: Pairwise summation bound for nonnegative inputs

source_locations.role: for nonnegative inputs, the sum of absolute values equals the sum

targets.informal_statement_paraphrase: For a power-of-two list of nonnegative real inputs, the absolute error of pairwise rounded summation is at most gamma at the tree depth times the exact sum.
targets.informal_proof_paraphrase: Every input passes through exactly r rounded additions, so the general pairwise bound uses gamma at r. Nonnegative inputs satisfy absolute value x_i equals x_i, which removes the absolute values from the exact sum.
targets.copyright_note: This is a benchmark-author paraphrase, not a quotation from the paper.

lean_target.statement_summary: The shared pairwise result is bounded by gamma u r times the ordinary sum when every input is nonnegative.
lean_target.binding_status: path, declaration, content hash, and clean N/L target builds fixed

targets.tier_reason: NumStability already proves the general pairwise absolute-value bound. The library-side proof should mainly find that theorem, use an adapter to the shared model, and simplify absolute values using nonnegativity.
targets.gold_proof_policy: A private construction proof may be kept under paper_bencmark/scratch_pad/private_gold/P01/. That path must never be mounted in an evaluation container.

targets.title: Compare the pairwise and recursive error bounds

source_locations.anchor: equation (3.6) and the paragraph immediately following it
source_locations.role: pairwise bound and comparison with the recursive bound

targets.informal_statement_paraphrase: For n = 2^r inputs, both standard forward-error bounds hold, and the pairwise coefficient gamma at r is no larger than the recursive coefficient gamma at 2^r minus 1.
targets.informal_proof_paraphrase: Apply the pairwise and recursive bounds. Then use r at most 2^r minus 1, validity at the larger index, and monotonicity of gamma to compare the two coefficients. The claim compares proven bounds, not the two actual errors on every input.
targets.copyright_note: This is a benchmark-author paraphrase, not a quotation from the paper.

lean_target.statement_summary: A conjunction of the pairwise bound, the recursive bound, and gamma u r <= gamma u (2^r - 1).
lean_target.binding_status: path, declaration, content hash, and clean N/L target builds fixed

targets.tier_reason: The result needs two summation theorems, arithmetic showing r <= 2^r - 1, transfer of the gamma validity condition, and monotonicity of gamma. No one existing declaration states the whole combined result.
targets.gold_proof_policy: A private construction proof may be kept under paper_bencmark/scratch_pad/private_gold/P01/. That path must never be mounted in an evaluation container.

targets.title: Recursive-summation running error in the no-guard-digit model

source_locations.role: the weaker addition model with separate errors on the two inputs
recursive-summation error as a sum of local no-guard errors
absolute running-error bound using computed prefixes and new inputs

targets.informal_statement_paraphrase: Under the no-guard addition model, recursive-summation error is at most u times the sum, from the second input onward, of the computed previous-sum size plus the new-input size.
targets.informal_proof_paraphrase: At each step, equation (5.1) makes the new error equal to the old error plus the computed prefix times alpha and the new input times beta. Sum these local errors as in (5.2), then use their u bounds and the triangle inequality to obtain (5.3).
targets.copyright_note: These are benchmark-author paraphrases of the printed equations, not quotations from the paper.

lean_target.statement_summary: The shared no-guard recursive sum is bounded by u times equation (5.3)'s computed-prefix running budget.
lean_target.binding_status: path, declaration, content hash, and clean N/L target builds fixed

targets.tier_reason: Equation (5.3) depends on actual computed prefix sums. NumStability has no accumulated no-guard recursive running-budget theorem. Condition L has useful pieces, including a one-step no-guard identity and a generic local-error recurrence scaffold, but it still needs new no-guard state, indexing, witness, and budget bridges or a fresh full induction.
targets.gold_proof_policy: A private construction proof may be kept under paper_bencmark/scratch_pad/private_gold/P01/. That path must never be mounted in an evaluation container.

targets.title: VecSum preserves the exact sum
targets.informal_statement_paraphrase: One pass of the error-free vector transformation leaves the exact total unchanged.
targets.informal_proof_paraphrase: Each TwoSum step replaces two values by a high and low pair with the same exact sum; iterating this local identity proves the vector invariant.
targets.copyright_note: This is a benchmark-author paraphrase, not a quotation from the paper.

targets.title: Sum2 doubled-working-precision error bound

source_locations.role: Sum2 absolute forward-error bound and proof

targets.informal_statement_paraphrase: Sum2 error is at most unit roundoff times the exact-sum magnitude plus gamma at N minus one squared times the input absolute mass.
targets.informal_proof_paraphrase: Combine the low-component budget, ordinary summation of those lows, exact preservation, final rounding, and the paper's gamma inequality.
targets.copyright_note: This is a benchmark-author paraphrase, not a quotation from the paper.

targets.title: Optimized K-fold dot-product error bound
targets.informal_statement_paraphrase: Without multiplication underflow, DotK has an absolute error bounded by the final-rounding term plus a Kth-order transformed-dot-product term.
targets.informal_proof_paraphrase: Build the exact length-2N transform and its absolute-mass bound, apply SumK at K minus one, and prove the gamma comparisons leading to equation (5.10).
targets.copyright_note: This is a benchmark-author paraphrase, not a quotation from the paper.
